wa_dark_side_of_liberty.notes: Starts at the top of the car-sized chockstone at the base of the east face. The first bolts are on slightly funky rock with yellow and orange lichen, but quality improves by the third bolt and the last five bolts are on superb granite. The climbing builds steadily on a steep, exposed face to a cryptic, steep crux (about V6) just below the anchor.

Almost no easy ground. The first half works up and around a vertical orange dike on interesting holds, leading into a short horizontal roof that needs blind reaches and heel hooks. Above the roof the angle eases only a little, with insecure moves to a small stance at the anchor.

An easier pitch before the crux. Leave the belay to the left, round the arete, and follow a brief, easy hand crack up to a bigger arete. A few moves are awkward and harder than they look, especially for shorter climbers.

The showpiece. Scramble left up the ramp to a little flake, climb past a few bolts of bouldery moves, then reach across right to where the finger crack begins. Layback and jam the roughly 45-foot crack to a good jug flake and rest. From there small feet and crimps lead over the bulge in a V9/V10 boulder problem, finished with a mantel onto a short slab. Without beta or chalk it can feel much harder than its grade.

Wander up the slab toward the big corner and the roof above it. Most of the pitch goes by jamming or laybacking on solid holds. It steepens before a traverse out and right around the offwidth roof; undercling and layback the offwidth until it is possible to squeeze inside, where feet and hands are good and the climbing quickly eases. A single #3 from the gear list is needed only on this pitch.

A short stretch of 4th class leads to a bolt by a tree, where the belay is moved. Climb left up a ramp, mantel up and right onto the top of a large flake, and set a few small cams before committing to insecure, awkward jams. The difficulty tapers off and better locks appear higher.
Straight up small ledges through some loose rock, a bit runout but never hard. Gain the huge open corner and turn right onto fun, easy laybacking.

Jam and stem up the overhanging open chimney on its left side until you can stem out to the right. Stay off the big wedged block close to the pitch's end, and build the belay on the bolts out left so the rope does not pinch behind that block.

A few wide stems up the chimney reach the first bolt; from there move left around the arete. Pleasant, easy face climbing trends up and left toward the arete separating the east face from the north, where the route meets Thin Red Line. Can be linked with pitch 10 if little gear is placed.

Easy ground over loose blocks, a little left of the arete, finishes the route. From here the choice is about 150 m of 4th-class terrain to the true summit, or rappelling the route on a single 80 m rope; the anchors on the route were placed roughly 40 m apart.

wa_lexington_tower_east_face.notes: Crack system then a left traverse into slopey climbing with tricky pro placements.
Up and slightly right to the base of an obvious left-facing corner; tree belay.
Climb the left-facing corner to a ledge with a tree belay.
Up and left through hand-to-finger cracks to a stance below a roof and a dead-end chimney.
Route crux: an exposed no-hands traverse right for 30 feet, then a difficult lieback into a hand/finger crack.
Offwidth climbing past a jammed 2x4 (fixed pro) and two bolts to an alcove.
Short chimney leads to blockier terrain and another offwidth section.
Easier low-fifth-class rock trending up and left past a few blocky steps; many parties simul-climb this section to save time before the upper headwall.
Continue on moderate terrain toward a tree belay.
Exposed catwalk traverse to the notch below the true summit, where the route unropes for the walk-off descent.

wa_garfield_mountain_preiss_route.notes: From the large ledge near the waterfall streaks, climb about 80 ft up the obvious stair-stepped rock gully to a crack anchor.
Exit the gully slightly right, then a full pitch of fun slabby rock with a few good cracks and pockets for solid gear. Belay on a shelf with a couple of small pools and good belay cracks.
Angle left and up on easier rock to the base of the great slabs.
600-700 ft of sub-par, essentially unprotectable slab. Aim for the small, thick stubby tree on the upper rightish side of the face, then continue to the next small tree patch to belay.
Straight up more slabby rock to the large ledge under the steeper headwall — a great bivy ledge.
Traverse the big ledge to its left side and climb a fun blocky corner that ends at a small sandy notch.
A few difficult moves off the notch protected by a solid thin crack; the angle then relents to class 3 with small trees.
The last obstacle: a rock wall of about half a pitch on good rock with good protection.
Walk down and left through a small gap in the trees onto the gentle northern slope, hike around right and scramble the short back side of the sub-summit rock (4,804 ft).

wa_let_it_burn.notes: A few steep 5.7 moves along a broken ramp system heading right past a tree to a flat ledge below a vertical crack.
A thin-hands splitter crack for about 25 feet, then move left toward trees at the far end of the ledge.
The signature pitch: thin finger cracks to a V-slot, using flakes on the left over a roof with 'wild knobs,' then traversing past two bolts to a bolted anchor.
Knobs, fins, and thin cracks stepping right twice into new crack systems to a small ledge anchor.
A right-slanting slot leads to a powerful layback past an overhanging flake to a narrow ledge.
Hand-traverse left along a golden flake, then climb the overhanging corner, surmounting a steep bulge near the top.
Traverse right and follow a thin corner feature up lower-angle slabs to a belay beneath a prominent roof.
Face and knob climbing into a crack on the left side of an alcove, then around the roof's left edge to a ridge stance.
Blocky climbing along right-leaning cracks on the crest to the summit ridge, joining the West Face's walk-off.
